body.text: Friend 'froze' after Beau Lamarre-Condon asked what she would do if he said he 'killed somebody', court told
In short:
A friend of Beau Lamarre-Condon told the court the murder accused had asked what she would do if he said, "I killed somebody".
She also told the court he had asked, "Would you help me hide the body?" before then "laughing it off".
What's next?
The first week of the trial has wrapped up but is expected to go for three months.

Former Sydney police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon asked a friend, after a breakup with Jesse Baird, what she would do if he told her he killed someone, and whether she would help him hide the body, a jury has heard.
Mr Lamarre-Condon is standing trial after pleading not guilty to murdering Mr Baird and his new boyfriend, Luke Davies, with his service pistol inside Mr Baird's Paddington terrace in February 2024.

The Crown alleges he formed an obsessive and jealous infatuation with Mr Baird, with whom he had been romantically involved with in 2022 and parts of 2023, and allegedly stalked the television presenter, interfered with his phone and Instagram, and broke into his house at least twice.
Witness Georgia Cook met the defendant at a boat party in 2021 and became friends.
The NSW Supreme Court heard that in mid-April 2023, they spoke about Mr Lamarre-Condon and Mr Baird sending each other "breakup goodbye" messages after Mr Baird said he did not want anything serious.
Ms Cook said it left the defendant "very upset".
The following month, when Ms Cook had dinner with Mr Lamarre-Condon, he told her he had been watching Mr Baird from outside his house.
"One of the first things he said was, 'What would you do if I told you I killed somebody?'" she told the jury.
"I just froze. He said, 'Would you help me hide the body?'"
She said she replied 'No' because she would not want to be haunted, before Mr Lamarre-Condon "laughed it off", and told her he had not done that, but "did do something crazy".
"He told me he had been watching Jesse from the outside of Jesse's house and in that time he'd seen Jesse have sex with other men," Ms Cook said.
Watching from outside the house
Ms Cook said Mr Lamarre-Condon told her about another time where he had seen Mr Baird taking photos of other people with a polaroid camera, which Mr Lamarre-Condon had previously bought.
She said he told her he had kept watching, saw where Mr Baird left his key, broke into the house, stole the camera, and ate an Easter egg of Mr Baird's.
"He said there was something else he did, but he wouldn't tell me what it was, which concerned me,"
Ms Cook recalled being told that the behaviour of watching from outside the house was "definitely more than once".
"He told me he would drive his mum's car so Jesse wouldn't recognise the car and wear a black hoodie while he was watching them," she said.
Mr Lamarre-Condon has also pleaded not guilty to a charge of aggravated break and enter, related to an incident at the Paddington terrace in August 2023.
The Crown alleges during a break-in, he stole Mr Baird's wallet and phone, but Mr Lamarre-Condon's defence team says he had a key which Mr Baird had previously given him.
Court shown CCTV of accused's movements
Mr Lamarre-Condon's lawyers this week flagged an argument of self-defence in relation to the day of the alleged murders.
The Crown has told jurors, in an opening address, that Mr Lamarre-Condon activated a burner phone, used a hire car, and waited near the Paddington property for three hours on February 19, 2023.
On Friday, the court released compilations of CCTV which were played to jurors this week, showing Mr Lamarre-Condon's movements in the lead-up to the alleged murders.

The footage, which was among 14,000 hours of CCTV material collected during the investigation, according to the lead investigator's evidence, includes Mr Lamarre-Condon leaving home early on the morning of February 19, 2024.
In parts of the compilation, he is seen dressed as an Uber Eats delivery driver and wearing a helmet on the street near Mr Baird's home.
The Crown alleges he was in the area for three hours, waiting as two housemates left.
In the days prior, the footage also shows him picking out a surfboard bag at Westfield Miranda with a friend.
The prosecution said the purchase of the bag was part of his alleged planning of Mr Baird's murder, and he intended to use it to dispose of Mr Baird's body.
The Crown has foreshadowed evidence from the friend that Mr Lamarre-Condon, at the time, asked whether he thought he would fit inside it.
Footage from the evening before the alleged murders shows Mr Baird and Mr Davies at the Beresford in Surry Hills.
Their bodies were ultimately found at a rural area at Bungonia in surfboard bags.

The prosecution alleges he murdered Mr Baird in the kitchen by shooting him twice, before allegedly murdering Mr Davies, who was in a bedroom calling Triple Zero (000), to ensure there was not a witness.
The defence case flagged during an opening by John Stratton SC is that Mr Lamarre-Condon went to the home to collect possessions and did not expect anyone to be there.
Mr Stratton said it was his client's case that there were two separate struggles, both involving the service pistol he had with him, during which the weapon fired and fatally injured the young men.
The trial, which has now finished its first week, has an estimated duration of three months.
